title: Polar ↔ Rectangular
summary: Looping Pol/Rec with θ (or y) in Y. ~40 bytes.

body.text: M1/M2 students store this so they do not forget that θ lives in Y. First prompt M: 0 = Rec, anything else = Pol. Then two numbers. First pause is r or x; EXE then RCL Y is not needed because the program already pauses Y (θ or y).

body.label: Memory / run mode
body.text: ~40 bytes of the shared 680-byte pool. Create the slot in COMP, Deg (or Rad to match SET UP). Type ? → : ◢ Goto Lbl If Then from SHIFT 3 (P-CMD).
Question: Use this program to solve the case: Pol(3, 4) in Deg.
Question: Use this program to solve the case: Rec(5, 53.13°).
Example 3 (edge): Point on the negative x-axis
Question: Use this program to solve the case: Point on the negative x-axis.
Given: Pol(−2, 0) should give r = 2, θ = 180° (or −180° depending on range).

items: r = 2. 【EXE】 → 180 (or −180). Rec of that pair returns (−2, 0)

body.label: Pitfalls
body.text: Pol/Rec also exist as SHIFT + and SHIFT − without a program; the stored line is for repeated conversion in one Run. θ range is −180° < θ ≤ 180°.
